title: M/S D.K. Associates vs . on 13 February, 2012
full_text: M/S D.K. Associates vs . on 13 February, 2012 IN THE COURT OF SHRI ARUL VARMA : MM (SPECIAL COURT - 2) : DWARKA COURTS : NEW DELHI. Case Number. : 187/2008. Date of Commencement of Offence. : 11.10.2008. Date of Institution of Present Case. : 11.11.2008. M/s D.K. Associates Having its Office : 38, Devli Road, Khanpur Extn., Near Punjab National Bank, New Delhi. Through its Attorney Sh. Krishan Mishra. ... Complainant. Vs. Jai Pal S/o Sh. Giriwar R/o MCD Green Park, (South Zone), Ward No. 62, New Delhi. ... Accused. Offence Complained Of. : U/s 138 NI Act . Plea of the Accused. : Not Guilty. Case No. 187/2008. Page No. 1 of 20 Arguments Heard On. : 6.2.2012. Final Order. : Acquittal. Date of Judgment. : 13.2.2012. ­ :: JUDGMENT :: ­ 1. Vide this judgment, I shall dispose off the present complaint filed by the complainant u/s 138 Negotiable Instrument Act, 1881 (hereinafter referred to as the " NI Act "). At the outset, it would be apposite to refer to the aforesaid provision. The same is reproduced as below: ­ "138. Dishonour of cheque for insufficiency, etc., of funds in the account. ­ Where any cheque drawn by a person on an account maintained by him with a banker for payment of any amount of money to another person from out of that account for the discharge, in whole or in part, of any debt or other liability, is returned by the bank unpaid, either because of the amount of money standing to the credit of that account is insufficient to honour the cheque or that it exceeds the amount arranged to be paid from that account by an agreement made with Case No. 187/2008. Page No. 2 of 20 that bank, such person shall be deemed to have committed an offence and shall, without prejudice to any other provision of this Act, be punished with imprisonment for (a term which may be extended to two years), or with fine which may extend to twice the amount of the cheque, or with fine which may extend to twice the amount of the cheque, or with both: ­ Provided that nothing contained in this section shall apply unless: ­ (a) the cheque has been presented to the bank within a period of six months from the date on which it is drawn or within the period of its validity, whichever is earlier; (b) the payee or the holder in due course of the cheque, as the case may be, makes a demand for the payment of the said amount of money by giving a notice in writing, to the drawer of the cheque, (within thirty days) of the receipt of information by him from the bank regarding the return of the cheque as unpaid; and (c) the drawer of such cheque fails to make the payment of the said Case No. 187/2008. Page No. 3 of 20 amount of money to the payee or as the case may be, to the holder in due course of the cheque within fifteen days of the receipt of the said notice. Explanation. ­ For the purposes of this section, "debt or other liability" means a legally enforceable debt or other liability." 2. Brief facts as averred in the present complaint are that the complainant is a registered firm under the Partnership Act and is engaged in the business of providing loan, finance assistance, leasing and hire purchases etc. and is having its office at the address as given in the memo of parties and the complaint has been filed by the authorized representative. The case of the complainant is that the accused had approached the complainant for taking a loan. That in lieu of discharge of his liability, the accused issued the a cheque bearing no. 401727 dated 26.8.2008 drawn on State Bank of India, Dakshinpuri, New Delhi in favour of the complainant with assurance that the same shall be encashed as and when presented. The complainant has further averred that the said cheque on presentation, got dishonoured due to the reason "funds insufficient". The Case No. 187/2008. Page No. 4 of 20 complainant thereafter issued a legal demand notice but despite service of the same, the accused neither replied to the notice nor paid the cheque amount in question. Hence, the complainant has filed the present complaint to prosecute the accused u/s 138 NI Act. 3. The complaint was filed within limitation on 11.11.2008 pursuant to which summons were issued against the accused, consequent thereupon the accused entered appearance and was admitted to bail. Notice was framed against the accused to which the accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. Thereafter, the matter was listed for evidence. 4. The complainant led its evidence by examining CW1 (authorized representative of the complainant) and has relied upon the following exhibited documents namely: authority letter as Ex CW1/A, cheque in question as Ex CW1/B, cheque return memo as Ex CW1/C, legal notice as Ex CW1/D, India post receipt and UPC receipt as Ex CW1/E and Ex CW1/F, the present complaint as Ex CW1/G and pre summoning evidence Case No. 187/2008. Page No. 5 of 20 as Ex CW1/H. In his affidavit, complainant has reiterated the facts as mentioned in the complaint. CW1 was cross examined by the accused. 5. In his statement u/s 313 CrPC accused has admitted availing of loan and issuance of cheque in question. Further, accused submits that he had issued the cheque in question as security. Accused had denied receiving of legal demand notice. 6. The accused led his examination in chief and was cross examined by the complainant as DW1. Accused had also examined Sh. Govind Ram, COP, Punjab National bank, Khan Pur, Delhi and Sh. Sudershan Ram, Post Master, Tis Hazari Post Office, Delhi. 7. From the evidence of both the parties and their respective arguments, the following points arise for my determination: ­ Case No. 187/2008. Page No. 6 of 20 S. DECISION POINTS FOR DETERMINATION NO. THEREON A Whether the cheque was drawn for discharge, in Negative. whole or in part, of any legally enforceable debt or other liability? B Whether statutory notice u/s 138 NI Act in writing Affirmative. was given to the drawer of the cheque making a demand for the payment of amount mentioned in the cheque withing 30 days of the receipt of information by payee/holder in due course from the bank regarding the return of the cheque as unpaid? C Whether Ex CW1/D is a legal valid notice as per Affirmative. the requirements of Section 138 NI Act? D Whether the drawer failed to make such payment Affirmative. withing 15 days of the receipt of the aforesaid notice? E What order? As per final Order. Case No. 187/2008. Page No. 7 of 20 STATEMENT OF REASONS FOR THE DECISION 8. Coming to the point regarding the issuance of cheque for discharge of legal debt or liability, counsel for complainant has contended that the accused had approached the complainant for a loan which was duly disbursed to him and whereupon the accused agreed and undertook to make payment of installments (EMIs) towards repayment of loan taken from the complainant. It is the case of the complainant that the accused in discharge of his liability issued a cheque bearing no. 401727 dated 26.8.2008 for an amount of Rs. 95,000/­ with the assurance that the said cheque would be encashed upon presentation. 9. Counsel for complainant averred that a loan was granted to the accused in the year 2005. On 21.11.2005, a loan agreement was executed between the parties. Ex CW2/1 is the loan agreement which makes it explicit that the accused did avail a loan from the complainant. It has been further alleged that the accused never paid the dues and a compromise was entered into between the parties and the cheque in question has been issued towards Case No. 187/2008. Page No. 8 of 20 the same. 10. Further, a perusal of the cross examination of the accused wherein he has avowed that "I do not have any receipt which shows that I had paid Rs. 84,000/­ to the complainant." would demonstrate that the accused has failed to prove that he did not owe any liability towards the complainant. 11. There are two presumptions of law as mandated by the Negotiable Instruments Act . According to Section 118 (a) it shall be presumed that every negotiable instrument was made or drawn for consideration. By virtue of this clause, the Court is obliged to presume that the promissory note was made for consideration or until the contrary is proved. In Mallavarapu Kasivisweswara Rao Vs. Thadikonda Ramulu Firm and Others AIR 2008 SC 2898 it was held as under: ­ "12. Under Section 118 (a) of the Negotiable Instruments Act, the court is obliged to presume, until the contrary is proved, that the promissory note was made for consideration. It is also a settled Case No. 187/2008. Page No. 9 of 20 position that the initial burden in the regard lies on the defendant to prove the non­existence of consideration by bringing on record such facts and circumstances which would lead the Court to believe the non­existence of the consideration either by direct evidence or by preponderance of probabilities showing that the existence of consideration was improbable, doubtful or illegal. ... ... ... The bare denial of the passing of the consideration apparently does not appear to be any defence. Something which is probable has to be brought on record for getting the benefit of shifting the onus of proving to the plaintiff. To disprove the presumption, defendant has to bring on record such facts and circumstances upon consideration of which the court may either believe that the consideration did not exist or its non­existence was so probable that a prudent man would, under the circumstances of the case, shall act upon the plea that it did not exist. ... ... ..." 12. According to Section 139 of NI Act "it shall be presumed, unless the contrary is proved that the holder of a cheque received the cheque for discharge in whole or in part, of any debt or other liability." Under Section 139 NI Act there is a legal presumption that the cheque was issued for discharging an antecedent liability and that presumption can be rebutted only Case No. 187/2008. Page No. 10 of 20 by the person who draw the cheque. This presumption can be rebutted by the accused by adducing evidence. So the burden of proof is on the accused. In Hiten P. Dalal Vs. Bratindranath Banerjee AIR 2010 SC 1898 it was held as under: ­ "11. The words 'unless the contrary is proved' which occur in this provision ( Section 139 ) make it clear that the presumption has to be rebutted by 'proof' and not by a bare explanation which is merely plausible. 13. To rebut the mandatory presumption operating against him, accused had vehemently contended that he had repaid the amount of Rs. 84,000/­ to the complainant and, therefore, there was no due outstanding against him. Counsel for accused has invited the Court's attention to the cross examination of CW1 wherein the AR of complainant had stated that "Also, 2 blank cheques as security are taken from the borrower.". It is the contention of the accused that the cheque in question is one of these blank cheques. Case No. 187/2008. Page No. 11 of 20 14. A perusal of the following statements made in the cross examination of the AR would also been relevant: ­ "Vol. The accused made some payments towards the discharge of loan. Thereafter, accused approached us for settling the amount, and asked for return of the 2 security cheques. Both these cheques were returned and the accused filled one of these cheques as per terms of settlement and gave this cheque back to us." 15. Further a perusal of the complete statement made in the cross examination of the accused would reveal that even though the accused did not have any 'receipt' which would show that Rs. 84,000/­ was paid to the complainant, a diary Ex DW1/A (colly) would evince the factum of such payment. Moreover, a comparison of the signature on the power of attorney and on certain pages of the diary Ex DW1/A would reveal that the signatures endorsed are similar/identical. It seems that certain payments were made by the accused and were duly received by the complainant/agent of the complainant. The onus would shift on the complainant in this regard. Moreover, it has not Case No. 187/2008. Page No. 12 of 20 been made clear as to how the accused came to indebted to the complainant for a sum of Rs. 95,000/­. 16. Further, counsel for accused has strongly contended that if at all the cheque in question was issued towards the settlement amount after a compromise was arrived at, then where is the proof of such compromise. This Court find force in the contention of the counsel for accused in as much as counsel for complainant has not been able to produce proof of any such compromise. 17. In view of the ratio decidendi in the judgment passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Krishna Janardhan Bhat Vs. Dattatraya G. Hedge , (2008) 4 SCC 54, the prosecution must prove the guilt of an accused beyond reasonable doubt whereas the standard of proof on the part of the accused is "preponderance of probabilities". It is apparent that the accused has furnished cogent reasons which resulted in shifting the burden of proof on the complainant, which the latter failed to discharge. Case No. 187/2008. Page No. 13 of 20 18. The burden was on the accused to disprove the presumption u/s 139 NI Act, a burden which he has successfully discharged. Thus, the complainant has not been able to prove that the cheque was issued for discharge of legal debt or other liability. 19. The complainant has further contended that in spite of giving of statutory notice u/s 138 NI Act, the accused failed to pay the amount of cheques in question. The accused, on the other hand, has vehemently denied the receipt of any legal notice. In his statement u/s 313 CrPC he has avowed that he never received the mandatory legal demand notice as stipulated by Section 138 NI Act. 20. The complainant has placed reliance on legal notice dated 26.9.2008 which is Ex CW1/D, postal receipts Ex CW1/E and Ex CW1/F. The address of the accused in the legal demand notice and the UPC was given as MCD Green Park (South Zone), Ward No. 62, New Delhi. A perusal of the vakalatnama filed of behalf of the accused reveals that the aforesaid address Case No. 187/2008. Page No. 14 of 20 in the legal notice is identical with the address mentioned in the vakalatnama filed on behalf of the accused. 21. At this juncture, it would be pertinent to refer to Section 27 of the General Clauses Act which is extracted as below: ­ "27. Meaning of service by post. ­ Where any Central Act or Regulation made after the commencement of this Act authorizes or requires any document to be served by post, whether the expression serve or either of the expressions give or send or any other expression is used, then, unless a different intention appears, the service shall be deemed to be effected by properly addressing, pre­ paying and posting by registered post, a letter containing the document, and, unless the contrary is proved, to have been effected at the time at which the letter would be delivered in the ordinary course of post." 22. Also a reference to the following paragraphs of judgment given by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in CC Alavi Haji Vs. Palapetty Muhammed & Another , Appeal (Crl.) 767 of 2007 would be relevant at this juncture: ­ Case No. 187/2008. Page No. 15 of 20 "14. Section 27 gives rise to a presumption that service of notice has been effected when it is sent to the correct address by registered post. In view of the said presumption, when stating that a notice has been sent by registered post to the address of the drawer, it is unnecessary to further aver in the complaint that in spite of the return of the notice unserved, it is deemed to have been served or that the addressee is deemed to have knowledge of the notice. Unless and until the contrary is proved by the addressee, service of notice is deemed to have been effected at the time at which the letter would have been delivered in the ordinary course of business. ... ... ... 15. Insofar as the question of disclosure of necessary particulars with regard to the issue of notice in terms of proviso (b) of Section 138 of the Act, in order to enable the Court to draw presumption or inference either under Section 27 of the G.C. Act or Section 114 of the Evidence Act, is concerned, there is no material difference between the two provisions. In our opinion, therefore, when the notice is sent by registered post by correctly addressing the drawer of the cheque, the mandatory requirement of issue of notice in terms of Clause (b) of proviso to Section 138 of the Act stands complied with. ... ... ... It is then for the drawer to Case No. 187/2008. Page No. 16 of 20 rebut the presumption about the service of notice and show that he had no knowledge that the notice was brought to his address or that the address mentioned on the cover was incorrect or that the letter was never tendered or that the report of the postman was incorrect. ... ... ..." Thus, as there has been no rebuttal of this presumption by the accused, it is deemed that the legal demand notice was duly served upon him. 23. Counsel for accused has also challenged the legality of Ex CW1/D stating that the said notice is an invalid one. He has invited the Court's attention to paragraph no. 3 of the legal notice dated 26.9.2008. The same is reproduced herein as under: ­ "3. That you issued a cheque bearing no. 401724 on dated 26­08­2008, for the same of Rupees 95000/­ (Nanty {sic} Five Thousand only) drawn on State Bank Of India Branch Dakshinpuri, New Delhi. towards the discharge of your liability, to my client." Case No. 187/2008. Page No. 17 of 20 24. Counsel for accused states that the cheque in question bears no. 401727 but the legal notice sent to the accused was with respect to cheque bearing no. 401724. He states that since the accused was not aware of the particular cheque which was dishonoured, it would not have been possible for him to make payment with respect to same. Counsel for complainant, however, contends that this is a mere typographical error and should not prejudice the complainant. 25. The issue that needs to be ascertained is whether this defect in notice is a material issue or not? In Abdul Rehman Vs. Mohd. Hashan, IV (2006) BC 265 (Bom) it has been held as under: ­ "Only because there was a variation in the number of the cheque mentioned in the notice and in the body of the complaint if would be of no consequence when in the notice of demand the amount covered by the dishonoured cheque was correctly mentioned. In the case at hand, the complainant's notice had the necessary and material particulars regarding the Bank's name and the amount of the cheque. In case the accused wanted at all to comply with the same he could have Case No. 187/2008. Page No. 18 of 20 done it easily. As such, the complaint could not have been dismissed for mixing up the number and the date of the cheque as mentioned in the notice and the complaint." 26. A perusal of the aforesaid judgment reveals that a minor typographical error would not invalidate the legal notice especially when the amount of cheque and the name of the bank therein have been properly mentioned. Thus, the Ex CW1/D is a legal valid notice. 27. It is evident that the drawer has failed to make the payment of the cheque amounts in question within 15 days of the receipt of the aforesaid notice, thus, the present complaint u/s 138 NI Act has been initiated against the accused. 28. FINAL ORDER : ­ In view of the foregoing observations and in view of the evidence, documents put forth and arguments of both the parties, the accused is hereby acquitted for the offence Case No. 187/2008. Page No. 19 of 20 punishable u/s 138 NI Act. Announced in the open Court on 13.2.2012. (ARUL VARMA) MM (SPECIAL COURT­2), DWARKA COURTS, NEW DELHI Case No. 187/2008. Page No. 20 of 20
